item.title: SCP-5127:
item.content:encoded:
Since it seem like you really want to improve, I thought I would give you some info on what I noticed upon first glance:

  • There's some formatting issues with the image clipping into the top bar.
  • Capitalizing the words "containment breach".
  • The huge amount of blinding blackboxes (I suggest you read this document to use them in a more pertinent way.)
  • Calling everything "massive."
  • Calling everything "proven." (Both of these things are fine, but they are written repetitively, imo.)
  • The D-Class having weirdly casual behavior.
  • The lack of a narrative (you have an MTF shoot at it and nothing happens, that's about it for story.)

It's basically an object that does a thing with a bit of "gore for the sake of gore" thrown in for flavor, I suggest you take this idea back to the drawing board and visit the Ideas Critique Forum before posting again and I highly encourage you to follow through the process of feedback and criticism to make a better anomaly the next time.

item.title: Meeting Anderson:
item.content:encoded: I can not help but read Jeffery as three syllables. Jeff-er-y. Darn you alternate spellings! In any case, echoing what has already been said, except I had significantly less background on Anderson's build up before reading this. I just know that what I see here is very good. I like him much more than I did — not because I didn't like him, but because I didn't know him at all.

item.title: Finding Anderson:
item.content:encoded: I know I am very, very late to this series, but this reveal of Anderson made me like him quite a lot. I imagine him (so far) as having English not be his first language, even though by the text of the story it most likely is. I just like the tinge of slower speaking, and the searching of "the bee's knees", as read with him having a slight yet unplaceable accent. Also, kind of saw the Amur unit coming, and that was fantastic, heheh.

item.title: Justice:
item.content:encoded: Looks like what I might have wanted to say has been said, so I'll keep it very brief. Art is great! I personally didn't care that the scientist was a lizard, though I 100% understand how people would have found that distracting. Story felt very bland to me, so I novoted, because I would have downvoted the story alone and upvoted the art alone so combined it cancels out. Excited to see what you come up with in the future, though. You're clearly quite talented.

item.title: SCP-052: Re: Who wrote this?
item.content:encoded: As a general note, you can usually check authorship of a page via the "History" link at the bottom of the main article (not the discussion page). Usually the author of iteration 0 (the posting of the page) is the author.

Thanks! I do think the confession is a bit heavy, but the hints throughout just weren't doing it for some reviewers so I decided to err on the side of caution. I have faith in the readers, but I also have faith in people getting irritated if they don't get what happened, so I split the difference.

item.title: SCP-5866:
item.content:encoded:
For the most part I enjoyed this enough to upvote. The characterization of Nass and Corbin was nice, albeit somewhat quick. The conversations between 5866 and Corbin was probably my favorite part of this. They bounced off of each other nicely and the dialogue from 5866 had that ancient being flair while not straying far from modern speech patterns.

My main issue with this is the confession log. It feels a bit exposition-dumpy to me. I know that Corbin’s plan had to be explained else 5866 reanimating wouldn’t have made sense, but it felt convenient that she just spills everything out in three paragraphs. Maybe that’s a personal thing and I can’t think of an alternate way you could have potentially done the reveal.

Regardless, I had fun reading this.
